corrections: Real tagged/flattened JSON key-map decoding defect fixed with canonical string-key deserialization; valid mapping delivered in accepted native/UI runs.
Real shutdown race let private-tagged UP escape after unhook. Current native v3 queue fence and fallible shutdown validated by actual window messages and truthful timeout cases.
F10 menu freeze, same-user Studio manual override assumption, and asynchronous Manual UP/Studio DOWN baseline were fixture/expectation corrections; affected aggregates retain NOT ACCEPTED.
Apply access policy intentionally revokes clients. Connected prefix stays NOT ACCEPTED; focused tail establishes a fresh actor and proves the remaining delayed scope boundary.

Own Python fixture preparation was corrected with app-owned mode configuration, bounded unfiltered message batches, and a bounded retry for the recorded report-file replacement race; product timeout assertions were unchanged.
limits: No hardware/RustDesk input used for control or validation; no OS input injection; only owned application pixels were captured.
No desktop-wide or independent same-process multi-user isolation, full MouseMux Ultra parity, arbitrary application/message-pump compatibility, or complete VK-range claim.
Fixed-process assigned output conversion is not exercised by this group; native feature coverage is automatic concurrent routing.

Fence success is accepted only for ordinary unfiltered message retrieval. Selected-range PM_REMOVE can overtake earlier UP messages; marker receipt alone does not prove their normalization or processing.
Non-pumping and PM_NOREMOVE timeout truthfulness tested on an owned x64 Python target. x86 positive plain-UP Stop tested; x86 timeout and forced native API failures are not tested.
Shared-process keyboard ownership tests prove first-down/last-up accounting, not independent same-process application isolation.

Historical groups were not broadly replayed. Current cleanup/connected boundaries target the changed transport and output behavior; earlier accepted feature evidence remains explicitly tied to its earlier image hashes.
